intended_object: This is the van Kampen diagram for an indexed family of opens U_i in a space X, viewed in Cat. Over the pairwise index category, it sends each i to the fundamental groupoid Π₁(U_i) and each pair (i, j) to Π₁(U_i ∩ U_j). Each map is the functor induced by the inclusion U_i ∩ U_j → U_i or U_i ∩ U_j → U_j. I took this from the docstring and from the companion definition `openCoverDiagram` in the same module.
explanation:
The body composes `openCoverDiagram U` with Mathlib's forgetful functor `Grpd.forgetToCat`. `openCoverDiagram U` is Mathlib's `Pairwise.diagram U`, followed by `Opens.toTopCat` and then `fundamentalGroupoidFunctor`. On objects this gives Π₁(U_i) for each i and Π₁(U_i ∩ U_j) for each pair (i, j). On morphisms it gives the functors induced by the two inclusions of an intersection into its charts. The file's simp lemmas, proved by `rfl`, confirm exactly this.

So the definition is the docstring's "same pairwise diagram, regarded as a diagram in the category of categories". This is the diagram whose colimit is the subject of the groupoid van Kampen theorem (May, Ch. 2 §7).

The setting is already general: any topological space, any index type, and any family of opens, with no connectedness or covering hypotheses. The universes `Cat.{u,u}` are the ones forced by `FundamentalGroupoid X` for `X : Type u`. Mathlib has no ready-made version of this diagram. It only provides the building blocks used here: `Pairwise.diagram`, `fundamentalGroupoidFunctor` and `Grpd.forgetToCat`.
